Connect to Perform

‘Connect to Perform’ is the philosophy that forms the basis for Human Connection’s consultancy work. It demonstrates how teams and organizations can move towards a more effective and pleasant way of working by making (mutual) connections. To bridge the gap between ‘theory’ and ‘applying it yourself’, we have designed a game that is played with great success in organizations and during our open evenings.

Connect to Perform Culture Development

Connect to Perform: the game

During the game, using a fictional situation, you gain insight into the methodology and possible interventions to develop organizational culture and performance. It becomes clear how you can identify which development phase an organization (or team) culture is in. Based on practical examples, you playfully see what is needed to take the next development step and what things actually backfire.

You gain insight into about fifty different interventions applicable in work practice, to influence the behavior and culture of a team and organization. In short, in a few hours, you are interactively immersed in our successful approach on how to make more impact with your team.

Open Game Evening

As an introduction, we organize an open game evening several times a year, nowadays often online, where our relations and interested parties are welcome to get acquainted with this methodology. (participation is completely free and without further obligations) Via a login to our online learning portal, you get access to videos with explanations and background information. Moreover, experience shows that it is very interesting to exchange thoughts with people you didn’t know before, working in diverse organizations.

In organizations, we play the game (online or offline) in MT trajectories or leadership programs. We have different formats, depending on the time and interest of the target group, and we also customize the content of the game where necessary. The translation to the work context, in light of the organization’s strategy, and also the concretization ‘what will I do with it tomorrow’ are important parts of the debriefing and any follow-up.

The game can also be requested as a standalone workshop. Think of a half or full day, online or offline, for a group of 4 to 80 participants. For more information, please send an email to Jojanneke van Goïnga.
